newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ total overseas debt rises $0.2 bln in Sept qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ total overseas debt rises $0.2 bln in Sept qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's total overseas debt rose NZ$0.2 billion (0.3 percent) to NZ$76.4 billion between June 30 and September 30, Statistics New Zealand said on Monday.
Total overseas debt has risen NZ$5.7 billion (8.1 percent) since September 30, 1995.

SNZ said new net borrowings of NZ$1.05 billion were partly offset by exchange rate gains estimated at NZ$0.8 billion, resulting in a $0.25 billion rise in total overseas debt in the September quarter.
Official government sector overseas debt fell $0.7 billion to $22.7 billion, following a $1.5 billion rise in the June quarter.

"The official sector has continued to repay foreign currency debt, but increased foreign investment in official domestically issued securities (DIS) has caused official sector overseas debt to remain between $21 billion and $23 billion since March 1995,"
Corporate sector overseas debt rose $1.0 billion to $53.8 billion. It has risen in six out of the last seven quarters.

SNZ said increased deposits by non-residents in NZ banks, and more recently increased foreign holdings of corporate DIS, have been the major factors in rising corporate sector overseas debt in the past year.

Deposits and DIS increased $1.4 billion and $1.0 billion respectively during the quarter. Overseas holdings of DIS have risen strongly in the past four quarters, while overseas residents' deposits in financial institutions have continued the variable but general rise of the past three years.

Falls in loans, bills and bonds offset the rises in deposits and DIS during the quarter. Overseas debt issued as bills and bonds have continued to fall, while loans have remained between $21.5 billion and $23.5 billion since June 30, 1994.
New Zealand's overseas debt to GDP ratio at September 30 was 85.4 percent, compared with 84.2 percent at June 30 and 80.3 percent a year ago.
The overseas debt to GDP ratio has risen in four out of the last five quarters, which SNZ said reflected overseas debt coupled with lower economic growth over the past year.
